headline_marked: SK Hynix to invest [[$38.1 billion]] in two new South Korean chip factories
headline: SK Hynix to invest $38.1 billion in two new South Korean chip factories
summary: The memory chip giant is building new DRAM and NAND facilities to meet soaring AI demand, with production expected to begin in 2029.
details: SK Hynix, the world's second-largest RAM and NAND chip manufacturer, announced a massive $38.1 billion investment to construct two new memory chip facilities in South Korea. This significant expansion is driven by the explosive demand for memory products fueled by the ongoing AI data center boom.

The company plans to invest $24.9 billion in a Yongin fabrication plant dedicated to producing High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and other DRAM products. An additional $13.2 billion will be allocated to a Cheongju facility focused on manufacturing NAND storage chips.

The first cleanroom is slated to begin production as early as June 2029. SK Hynix officials stated that this investment decision was made after a thorough review of market demand and aims to capitalize on the market's growth trajectory.

The surge in demand for AI memory products has led to a significant increase in prices, benefiting companies like SK Hynix. However, this has also contributed to higher prices for consumer electronics such as smartphones, consoles, and PCs.

Despite some analyst concerns about a potential market bubble, SK Hynix is betting on the continued growth of the AI sector. However, with production not expected for several years, memory prices are unlikely to decrease before the end of 2028, according to Counterpoint Research.
